Paper: [Ren et al. (2015), Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.01497).

## Problem

[Fast R-CNN](fast-r-cnn.qmd) shares visual features but still obtains candidate regions from an external algorithm.
Faster R-CNN learns to propose regions from the same convolutional features used by its detection head.

## Previous Attempts

Selective search provides class-independent proposals without learning them jointly with the CNN features.
Fast R-CNN accelerates region classification but leaves proposal generation as a separate cost.
Faster R-CNN introduces a **region proposal network**, or RPN, and combines it with the Fast R-CNN detector. [Sections 1–3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.01497#page=2).

## Proposed Solution

A sliding network reads each spatial position of the shared convolutional feature map.
At each position, predefined reference boxes called **anchors** cover several scales and aspect ratios.
For $k$ anchors at a location, the original RPN predicts $2k$ object/background classification scores and $4k$ box offsets.
The classification target is objectness, not a semantic category such as cat or chair. [Section 3.1 and Figure 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.01497#page=3).

Predicted offsets refine anchors into proposals.
Proposal filtering and non-maximum suppression produce candidate boxes for the second-stage Fast R-CNN head, which performs semantic classification and further box refinement.
The architecture therefore has two detection stages even though its convolutional features are shared.

## RPN Targets and Loss

An anchor is positive if it has the highest IoU for a ground-truth box or has IoU above 0.7 with a ground-truth box.
A non-positive anchor is negative if its IoU with every ground-truth box is below 0.3; remaining anchors are ignored for this training loss.
The highest-overlap rule ensures a training match even when no anchor reaches the high threshold. [Section 3.1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.01497#page=4).

Let $p_i$ predict objectness, $p_i^*\in\{0,1\}$ be the label, and $t_i,t_i^*$ be predicted and target offsets.
Writing the two normalized terms separately,

$$
    \begin{aligned}
        L_{\mathrm{cls}}&=\frac1{N_{\mathrm{cls}}}
        \sum_i\ell_{\mathrm{bin}}(p_i,p_i^*),\\
        L_{\mathrm{reg}}&=\frac1{N_{\mathrm{reg}}}
        \sum_i p_i^*\sum_k\rho(t_{ik}-t_{ik}^*),\\
        L&=L_{\mathrm{cls}}+\lambda L_{\mathrm{reg}}.
    \end{aligned}
$$

The factor $p_i^*$ restricts box regression to positive anchors, and $\rho$ is [Fast R-CNN's Smooth L1 penalty](fast-r-cnn.qmd).
The normalization constants and weight determine the relative contribution of the terms. [Equation 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.01497#page=4).
The original RPN minibatch samples 256 anchors from one image, with at most half positive; unavailable positives are replaced by negatives rather than inventing a balanced set. [Section 3.1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.01497#page=5).

## What Joint Training Means Here

The paper presents a four-step alternating procedure to learn shared features between the proposal and detection networks.
It also discusses approximate joint training, which treats proposals as fixed when differentiating the detection loss.
That approximation omits the path through predicted proposal coordinates.
The shared backbone can still receive gradients from both losses. [Section 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.01497#page=6).

Consequently, “one network” does not mean that the original reported training differentiates exactly through every proposal-selection and coordinate operation.
Architecture sharing, a combined objective, and exact end-to-end derivatives are separate claims.

## Evidence and Limitations

The paper evaluates learned proposals, shared features, and final detection quality through its experiments and ablations. [Section 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.01497#page=6).
Anchor design, positive/negative assignment, proposal filtering, and the second stage remain explicit components.
[SSD](ssd.qmd) predicts categories and boxes directly from multiple feature maps, while [DETR](detr.qmd) uses learned prediction slots and one-to-one target matching.

## Connections

[R-CNN](r-cnn.qmd#box-regression) defines the offset parameterization, and its [IoU explanation](r-cnn.qmd#iou-nms) separates overlap measurement from suppression.
The [loss note](../../study-notes/machine-learning/loss.qmd#loss-and-risk) helps distinguish loss terms, their weights, and which examples contribute gradients.
